clue.text: Expert came first and was noisily animated

parts.note: crack as an adjective means expert, first-rate
someone who came first led the field

explanation.surface: A specialist arrived ahead of the others and was loudly lively about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech or a party that crackled was full of noisy energy and sparkle.

clue.text: One raving about the Church picked up as apostate?

indicators.note: the raving person's letters go about, around, the church letters

parts.note: a ranter is someone who raves and harangues

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the letters are lifted to read upwards

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A ranting preacher turns against the Church and is seen as a traitor to the faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate renounces a former belief, which is what a person who recants does.

clue.text: Beers about to be brought into nunnery? It's getting better!

indicators.note: the beer and about letters are placed inside the nunnery word

parts.note: a convent is a nunnery
ales are beers
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Smuggling beer into a convent gives the nuns a cheering recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: A convalescent patient is recovering, on the mend after illness.

clue.text: Outstanding achiever left with gold

parts.note: aureate means golden, gold-coloured

explanation.surface: A star performer sets off with a gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A laureate is someone honoured for exceptional achievement, as with a Nobel prize.

clue.text: Areas with the same limited electricity supply?

indicators.note: the word for the same is cut down to its short written form, losing its middle

parts.note: ditto means the same again
the mains supply electricity to a house

explanation.surface: Regions that share an identical rationed power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims DITTO to DO, the standard written abbreviation of ditto.
explanation.definitionFit: Domains are territories or spheres, areas of land or of activity.

clue.text: Barrier against a hard man in particular role

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A wall is set up against a tough guy in a specific job.
explanation.walkthrough: A WALLAH, from Hindi, is a person in charge of a particular job, as in 'tea wallah'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallah denotes someone with a given occupation or responsibility, a role-holder.

clue.text: Pole, a very good chess player losing queen

indicators.note: losing means the queen letters are dropped from the master

parts.note: a master is a highly rated chess player
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A chess expert loses their queen, a pole being a Polish player perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A mast is an upright pole, as on a ship.

clue.text: It may be collected by duster possibly

definitions.text: It may be collected by duster possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Dust and debris are what a duster gathers up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be collected by' just joins the pieces; IT and DUSTER together are rearranged, and the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is loose debris and waste, just what a duster picks up.

clue.text: The way the lazy may receive things such as food?

definitions.text: The way the lazy may receive things such as food?

parts.words: The way the lazy may receive things such as food?
parts.note: food served on a dish is literally given this way, and idle people like things handed to them without effort

explanation.surface: Idle people expect things handed to them like a served meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means received without any effort, like a meal brought to the table.

clue.text: Medical examination barely sufficient with time wasted

indicators.note: the time letter is lost, used up, from the word

parts.note: scant means barely enough

explanation.surface: A hospital check-up is hardly adequate because time is squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: A scan, such as an MRI or ultrasound, is an imaging examination in medicine.

clue.text: What could be arts used to produce heavenly body

parts.note: read as a clue, a changeable form of the word STAR could give arts, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what creative work might yield a celestial object.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, taken as an anagram instruction, turns STAR into 'arts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A variable star is a star whose brightness changes, a celestial object.

clue.text: Pass sham line off — an abuse of this?

definitions.text: Pass sham line off — an abuse of this?

indicators.note: off signals these letters are wrong, out of order

explanation.surface: Fobbing customers off with a fake patter is a misuse of the selling art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges PASS SHAM LINE; the whole clue also describes the answer being abused.
explanation.definitionFit: Salesmanship is the skill of selling, which passing off a sham line would abuse.

clue.text: The beatified Fitzgerald is some girl!

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is one beatified and then canonised
Ella Fitzgerald was the jazz singer

explanation.surface: A tribute to the saintly jazz singer Ella Fitzgerald as quite a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a girl's given name.

clue.text: There's nothing one can believe in

definitions.text: There's nothing one can believe in

parts.words: There's nothing one can believe in
parts.note: read as a creed, it says belief in nothing at all, the outlook of a total sceptic

explanation.surface: A despairing remark that no faith is worth holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A nihilist rejects all moral and religious principles, believing in nothing.

clue.text: Vandalised paintings etc, brought back and dumped

indicators.note: brought back means the art word is read backwards

parts.note: art covers paintings and the like
to shed is to cast off, dump

explanation.surface: Artworks were returned and thrown away after being wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A place trashed by vandals has been wrecked or damaged.

clue.text: Like gaudy present? Little child hides disappointment

indicators.note: the child word wraps around and conceals the letters for disappointment

parts.note: a tiny is an informal word for a small child
a sell is a let-down, a disappointment

explanation.surface: A small child conceals their letdown at a flashy gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinselly means showy and cheap, like a gift decked in tinsel.

clue.text: Killer of mother held in poorest esteem

indicators.note: held in signals the answer is contained within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A matricide is someone held in very low regard.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Orestes killed his mother Clytemnestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Orestes avenged his father Agamemnon by slaying his mother Clytemnestra.

clue.text: Muse, taking drink at home — tea possibly?

parts.note: rum is a drink
in means at home

indicators.note: possibly signals the tea letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pondering things over a drink at home, maybe with tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to ponder or meditate, the same as to muse.

clue.text: Eastern maiden, I have to be radiant

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A girl from the East declares she means to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Emissive means giving out radiation or light, so radiant.

clue.text: Fills in form for job? A couple of pages with untruths!

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for pages
lies are untruths

explanation.surface: A two-page job application packed with falsehoods.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who applies submits an application, filling in a form for a post.

clue.text: Let a handle slip when talking

definitions.text: Let a handle slip when talking

parts.words: Let a handle slip when talking
parts.note: a handle is slang for a name, and letting one fall casually into conversation is to show off acquaintance

explanation.surface: Someone loses grip of a handle while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention famous people casually to impress, slipping their names into talk.

clue.text: Somewhat dry fruit is immersed in water

indicators.note: the word is is placed inside the water word

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A dried fruit gets soaked in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a fruit with most of its moisture gone.

clue.text: Aim that is set down by spiteful person

parts.note: to mean is to intend, to aim
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A goal written down by someone nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is an informal word for an unkind, petty person.

clue.text: UK region saddens Tamil resettling

indicators.note: resettling means the letters move to new positions

explanation.surface: A Tamil relocating to part of England is saddened by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The East Midlands is an English region including Nottingham and Leicester.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Midlands is one of the official regions of England.

clue.text: Seat given new foundation becomes squashy

indicators.note: in a down entry the foundation is the bottom letter, which is replaced

parts.note: a sofa is a seat

explanation.surface: A chair with a new base turns out squidgy.
explanation.walkthrough: SOFA's last letter, its foundation in a down entry, is swapped for T; the clue does not say which letter goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft means yielding to pressure, squashy.

clue.text: One taken in by the woman who is out to succeed?

indicators.note: the letter for one is enclosed by the woman word

parts.note: her refers to a woman
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man ensnared by a woman with ambitions to get on.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person in line to succeed to a title or estate.

clue.text: Fifty-one needed by cat? Just eight more than this one

definitions.text: Just eight more than this one

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: A cat needs fifty-one, being only eight beyond this one.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat has nine lives, eight more than the single one a palm's line of life suggests; the definition is cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's nine lives exceed by eight the one life traced in palmistry.

clue.text: Fish swirling round landing stage not so alert

indicators.note: swirling round means the fish word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: eels are fish
a pier is a landing stage for boats

explanation.surface: Fish circle a jetty, rather drowsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepier means drowsier, less wide awake.
